messages:
mike: Ran the batcher/allocator simulator overnight with the new hysteresis heuristic. Results attached below, TL;DR: fewer kernel switches, fewer transient OOMs, ~6% end-to-end p50 latency win for mixed short/long workloads. @emma can you eyeball the profiler traces when you have a sec?

mike: command I used:
```
./ws-sim --profile --trace-kernels --batcher=work-stealing --hysteresis-ms=25 --kv-reserve=8MB --kern-switch-th=0.15 
```

mike: notable trace snippets:
- frequent flashattn->triton flip at seq=768 boundary before hysteresis.
- with hysteresis we hold flashattn for an extra ~40ms causing fewer slab reallocs.
- cublaslt fallback triggered only on 2% of requests (large batch high padding)

emma: nice. Can you paste the tiny perf table? even rough numbers help.

mike: perf summary (mixed workload: 70% short 30% long, batch target 32):
```
baseline (no-hyst): p50=42.1ms p95=210ms kernel-switches/hr=720 oom-events=7
hyst-25ms:      p50=39.6ms p95=198ms kernel-switches/hr=180 oom-events=1
```

mike: also saw KV cache churn decreased — we were evicting a lot due to micro-reallocs. hysteresis reduced short-lived workspace allocations so KV objects lived longer.

raj: quick q: how does this interact with the kv-reserve knob? you set 8MB; did you test 0/16/32?

mike: yes ran 0/8/16: with 0 we saw 3 extra OOMs (edge cases when a long request and many short ones coincide). 16MB gave no extra benefit but increased baseline memory footprint. 8MB seems Pareto.

sophie: is the kernel-switch threshold the ratio of expected token work between kernels?

mike: it's a normalized delta in estimated workspace + runtime cost between best and fallback kernel. if delta < 0.15 we avoid switch unless hysteresis expired. reduces flip-flopping for borderline seq lengths.

emma: nice heuristic. can we land an A/B in canary? My worry: some customers with very peaky short bursts might prefer more aggressive switching to save memory. We should make it opt-in per-deployment.

mike: agreed. plan: default hyst=25ms, per-deploy override + operator flag to prefer memory-savers (aggressive-switch=true).

dev-bot: deploy-preview: canary=eng-runtime-canary-3 will run build #3723 with hyst=25ms and kv_reserve=8MB.

raj: one more datapoint — profiler showed cublaslt matmul kernel had ~12% higher L2 stall on the nodes that hit fallback. Might be fragmentation + different workspace alignment causing cache misses. worth a deeper look but low priority.

emma: noted. also ping @sophie to add a lightweight telemetry event: kernel_choice (chosen, alt, reason, seq_len, batch_size, kv_reserve) so we can correlate choices to observed OOMs. keep payload tiny.

sophie: on it. sending sketch in a sec.

sophie: sketch of event (proto):
```
{"ts":<now>, "chosen":"flashattn", "alt":"triton","reason":"runtime+ws","seq":512,"batch":16,"kv_reserve_kb":8}
```

mike: perfect. also adding a cheap tracer that increments a counter whenever we flip kernel choice inside a short window (flip_count) so we can detect oscillation.

emma: sounds good. after canary runs for 24h let's review oom-events and flip_count histograms. if flip_count>5 per minute we can relax threshold.

mike: ack. one last note: in a few traces we hit a pathological case where flashattn wins runtime but requests allocate a big FFN workspace that triggers cublaslt fallback later in the graph, leading to an OOM mid-inference. I'm adding a precheck that sums projected per-layer workspace and refuses kernel choice if subsequent layers would overflow slab. tiny patch in the allocator planner.

raj: good call. micro-atomic check avoids wasted flips.

emma: thanks all — excited to see if this reduces the 'mystery oom' support tickets. :thumbsup:

dev-bot: canary started: eng-runtime-canary-3 (build 3723). logs: https://ci.example.com/builds/3723

mike: leaving raw trace snippets here for later digging:
```
TRACE START ts=1738425610
[alloc] slab_alloc workspace 1.2MB -> flashattn chosen
[kernel] flashattn(seq=640,batch=24) runtime=18.3ms ws=1.2MB
[alloc] ffn_alloc 24.0MB -> would push slab over 95% -> decision: pre-check fail
[kernel] switch -> triton_ffn runtime+ws penalty=6.4ms
TRACE END ts=1738425658
```

emma: that pre-check snippet is gold. please add to the PR description.

mike: will do. end of thread.
